==============================================================================
SECTION 1. HOW TO READ THIS DOCUMENT
==============================================================================

[Keep this section word for word in every document, replacing only CASEID.]

This document explains, in plain language, how each judgment-based code for
this case was reached. A judgment-based code is one where reasonable
researchers could disagree, such as how severe an episode was or how it ended.
Facts such as dates and measures are recorded separately in the case's
extraction file ([CASEID]_JSON.json).

For each variable the document gives the code, the confidence level, whether a
person should check it, the facts it rests on, the steps of reasoning, the
strongest case for each option considered, and why one option was chosen.

Two cautions. First, this justification was written by an AI model. It is a
written argument that can be checked against the facts it cites. It is not a
record of how the model computed the code internally, and it is not proof that
the code is right. Second, codes marked for human review should be confirmed
by a person before they are used in analysis.

==============================================================================

   Confidence: [high / medium / low] | Human review: [yes / no]

SECTION 4. JUSTIFICATION BY VARIABLE

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CONFIDENCE: [high / medium / low]

  - [the codebook category or rule used]

FACTS THIS RESTS ON:
  - [fact in plain words] [extraction ID, e.g. E05]

HOW THE DECISION WAS REACHED:
  1. [first step of the reasoning] [extraction IDs]
  2. [next step]
  [Last step states the decision.]

[Include the next block for imposesanct_type and threatsanct_type only.]
HOW EACH MEASURE WAS ASSIGNED:
  - [measure ID] ([measure description]): [code and meaning, or "not coded
    separately"]. [reason]

THE OPTIONS CONSIDERED:
  [Up to three options, including the chosen one. If only one option is listed,
  say why no serious alternative exists.]
  Option A: [code and meaning] - [SELECTED / not selected]
      Best argument for it: [the strongest good-faith case for this code,
      written as its supporter would make it]
      Its weakest point: [the strongest objection to this code]

  Option B: [code and meaning] - [SELECTED / not selected]
      Best argument for it: [...]
      Its weakest point: [...]

WHY THIS DECISION WAS MADE:
  [Why the chosen code beats the alternatives. This same text appears, in
  shortened form, in the Coding Rationale section of the narrative.]

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT:
  [The evidence or ruling that would change the code]

SECTION 7. WHERE THIS APPEARS ELSEWHERE
==============================================================================

The reason each code was chosen also appears, in short form, in the Coding
Rationale section at the end of the case narrative. The facts cited by ID are
in the extraction file, and the codes themselves are in the codes file
([CASEID]_CODES.json).
